PROCEDURE CODE
Art 1278
The judgment or decree pronouncing the divorce has effect for the spouses from the day on which the decision acquires the force of res judicata and has effect for third parties from the day on which it is mentioned in the marriage certificate or the divorce certificate is drawn up.
For the spouses, as regards their property, there is retroactive effect to the day on which the action was brought and, where there is more than one action, to the day on which the first action was brought, whether or not it was successful.
If one of the spouses dies before an entry is made in the marriage certificate or the divorce certificate is drawn up, but after the judgment or decree granting the divorce has become res judicata, the spouses are considered to be divorced vis--vis third parties, subject to the suspensive condition of the entry in the marriage certificate or the drawing up of the divorce certificate.
The Family Court may, at the request of one of the spouses, if it deems it equitable due to exceptional circumstances specific to the case, decide in the judgment granting the divorce that the existence of certain assets built up or certain debts contracted since the de facto separation began shall not be taken into account in the liquidation of the community. The parties may also make such a request during the liquidation of the community.
